To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The surface discharge propagation field is determined by the filamentary channels of the surface corona discharge, till a critical value Vcrit of the applied voltage, beyond which the discharge is dominated by leader-like discharges, of higher conductivity, propagating above the surface.
the discharge is a gas discharge, and that the surface is a heat source for the discharge, which is a heat sink for the surface.
the surface discharges are gas discharges, propagating above the surface, and not surface discharges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the current distribution in ac discharges propagates at an air / solid interface and with the chemistry of the associated products.

the study of the current distribution of ac surface discharges, with the aim of determining the voltage range in which these discharges propagate and the associated chemistry, in order to better understand the mechanisms leading to the dielectric failure.

the study of the propagation fields and of the current density distribution for the surface discharges, as well as with the chemistry of the discharge products, with the aim of understanding the mechanisms of the discharge propagation and of the surface damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of ac surface discharges, there is no fundamental difference between corona, glow and leader discharges.
, in the case of a dielectric surface, the ac discharge is of corona type up to Vcrit and becomes of leader type beyond Vcrit.
the ac discharges at the air / dielectric interfaces are, at the beginning, corona-like and then leader-like discharges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the surface discharges are a combination of gas discharges propagations above a dielectric surface, and of a heat transfer between the gas channels and the dielectric surface, which, in turn, modifies the propagation fields.
, for the surface discharges, the gas is the primary medium for the propagation, and the surface is a secondary medium, with a secondary role in the propagation.

, in ac surface discharges, the filamentary discharge component, which is the most energetic one and which determines the discharge propagation, behaves like an air gap corona discharge, while the glow component is the one that determines the charge distribution on the surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in ac surface discharges, a large part of the discharge energy is transferred from the gas phase to the dielectric surface, where it is dissipated.
the surface discharges are not a simple extension of corona discharges, but a complex phenomenon involving the gas and the dielectric surface.

, for the same discharge voltage V, the surface discharge is more energetic than the gap discharge and that this is due to the heat transferred from the gas channels to the surface and then returned back to the gas.
